title: Open WebUI cache file serving -- T1005 startswith containment check without trailing separator
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54014 (GHSA-j2c8-v969-8r5c,
CVSS 4.3 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

`serve_cache_file()` in `open_webui/main.py` validates a requested
path against the cache directory with
`file_path.startswith(os.path.abspath(CACHE_DIR))` -- WITHOUT
appending `os.sep` to the comparison prefix. This is the classic
"prefix containment without a trailing separator" bug: a resolved path
landing in a SIBLING directory whose name merely begins with the same
characters as `CACHE_DIR` (the advisory's own examples: `cache_sibling`,
`cache_backup`, `cached_models`) passes the `startswith` check even
though it is not actually inside `CACHE_DIR` at all. Any authenticated
user can therefore read files from these sibling directories through
the cache-file endpoint.

Detection logic flags a cache-file-serving request whose resolved path
targets a directory sharing `CACHE_DIR`'s name PREFIX but not equal to
it followed by a path separator -- the exact shape the unpatched
`startswith` check incorrectly accepts.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact function, file, and vulnerable
comparison), fixed in 0.9.6 (adds the trailing separator to the
containment check).
